blocks.text: After the verb **помогать** the person to whom help or assistance is given is in the dative case: *Я помогаю ему. Она помогает брату.*
After the verb **обещать** the person to whom something is promised is in the dative case: *Капитан обещал старшине отпуск.*

The indirect object refers to objects that are not being directly acted upon. For example, 'I wrote a letter to you' - 'I' is the subject, 'a letter' is the object, and 'to you' is the indirect object.

Thus, in Russian, instead of saying 'to you', they say the word 'you' in its dative form: **Я пишу письмо *вам***. There are many common verbs that can have an indirect object, and most correspond with the English use of the word 'to':
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lessons 35, 36. From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Ты веришь ___ (этот слух, dat. pl.)?
exercises.why: **слух → слухам** (dat. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural слухи; declines like DLI's книги (guttural stem): D. книгам. Ending — (no ending) → -ам.  **этот → этим** (dat. pl., agreeing with слухам). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новые: D. новым. Ending -эти → -м (the stem changes: эти-).  Declension: sg. слух · слуха · слуху · слух · слухом · слухе; pl. слухи · слухов · слухам · слухи · слухами · слухах.  «For the dative and the prepositional plural there are two kinds of endings for each case: -ам, -ами, -ах after a hard, a sibilant or a guttural consonant; -ям, -ями, -ях after a soft consonant, a «ь» or a vowel. The formation of these cases does not depend upon the gender of the noun, but only upon the sound preceding the ending.» — DLI, Lessons 42–45.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: И почему-то показался он Наде ___ (серый, dat. pl.), провинциальным.
exercises.why: **серый → серым** (dat. pl., agreeing with its noun). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новые: D. новым. Ending -ые → -ым.  Declension (plural): серые · серых · серым · серые · серыми · серых.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Мы пьем спирт, и он дает ___ (мы, dat. pl.) веселье.
exercises.why: **мы → нам** (dat. pl.). Declension: мы · нас · нам · нас · нами · нас.  After a preposition the third-person pronouns take н-: у него, к ней, с ними. — DLI, Lessons 32 and 35.  — forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Простите, но вы, кажется, обещали ___ (я, dat. sg.) немного денег?.. — смущенно начал он.
exercises.why: **я → мне** (dat. sg.). Declension: я · меня · мне · меня · мной · мне.  After a preposition the third-person pronouns take н-: у него, к ней, с ними. — DLI, Lessons 32 and 35.  — forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Лев засмеялся, что мышь обещает ___ (он, dat. sg.) добро сделать, и пустил ее.
exercises.why: **он → ему** (dat. sg.). Declension: он · его · ему · его · им · нём.  After a preposition the third-person pronouns take н-: у него, к ней, с ними. — DLI, Lessons 32 and 35.  — forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).
